guard: no suite may spread the ambient environment into a child without first stripping the COTAL_ variables, and the frozen baseline of pre-existing spreads can only shrink
why: THIS CENSUS EXISTS BECAUSE TWO RUNTIME CELLS COULD NOT SEE THE DEFECT AND A REVIEWER NAMED THE
SHAPE THAT COULD. A suite that builds a child env as `{ ...process.env, ...ours }` hands that
child whatever identity the session running the suite happens to hold. Both instances found on
this branch were GREEN before the change, because the connector env layered on top overwrote the
very variables that would have revealed the inheritance.
N1 REMOVES ONE STRIP, from the suite where the defect was actually found. It must redden the
offenders assertion, which is the census's only real output. A census that cannot notice a strip
disappearing is a list, not a guard.
N2 IS THE RATCHET'S OWN TEETH. Freezing a baseline is only honest if the baseline is forced to
shrink; a frozen entry that stops spreading has to leave the list, or the waiver outlives the
thing it waived and the file quietly re-earns its exemption forever. Mutating a frozen entry's
spread away must therefore go RED on the stale-baseline assertion, not quietly pass.
NO BUILD STEP: the suite reads source files off disk and imports nothing from a built package, so
there is no dist/ copy that could disagree with the mutation.
N3 IS THE MIXED-FILE CASE. A file can strip one child and still spread ambient identity into another.
Per-file STRIP+DELETE treated that as clean, including when `delete` only appeared in comments.
Removing the auth-service strip while the CLI child still filters COTAL_ must redden user-spawn.
N4 PROVES THE REAL POPULATION IS ENUMERATED. Embedded examples can pass while the repository scan
quietly grades only the first spread in every file. Truncating spreadIndexes must red at the real
spread-count sentinel because real multi-spread files contain more spreads than classified files.
N5 PROVES OWNERSHIP IS STRUCTURAL, NOT INDENTATION. A process.env scrub at column zero can still
be nested inside an uncalled function or conditional block. Replacing brace-depth zero with a
column-zero test must red on the adversarial nested controls.
N6 PROVES LEXICAL-REGION OWNERSHIP. A scrub embedded in an unused child-script template cannot
license a later module-code spread, and a module scrub cannot license a spread in another literal.
Removing the same-region check must red on the unused-template control.
N7 PROVES REGEX LITERALS ARE TOKENIZED. Braces inside /{/, /}/, and /[{}]/ are data, while a
division slash remains code. Removing regex-region handling must red on the close-brace nested
control before a regex can collapse structural depth.
N8 PROVES TEMPLATE RAW TEXT HAS ITS OWN OWNER. Flattening raw text into interpolation code must
red before a raw-template scrub can license an interpolation spread.
N9 PROVES INTERPOLATION EXECUTES IN THE CONTAINING CODE REGION. Assigning it to the template's
raw-text owner must red before a module scrub can stop licensing its interpolation spread.
N10 PROVES INTERPOLATION CONTENTS ARE PARSED RECURSIVELY. Dropping that recursion must red before
an inner template scrub can be mistaken for containing module code.
N11 PROVES EVERY SIBLING INTERPOLATION IS PARSED. Limiting recursion to the final span must red
before a nested template scrub in one interpolation can clear a spread in its sibling.
N12 PROVES COOKED CHILD-SCRIPT MATCHES KEEP SOURCE COORDINATES. Replacing the mapping with
linear cooked offsets must red where an earlier escape would move a top-level scrub inside a brace.

mutations.name: N1 the opencode cooperative-stop suite loses its COTAL_ strip
mutations.find: for (const key of Object.keys(HOST_ENV)) if (key.startsWith("COTAL_") || key.startsWith("OPENCODE_")) delete HOST_ENV[key];
mutations.expectRed: spread the ambient environment into a child without stripping COTAL_ first
mutations.note: The exact regression the census exists to stop: this file is where the live-identity capture was found, and without the strip it is an offender again.

mutations.name: N2 a frozen baseline entry stops spreading and is left on the list
mutations.expectRed: FROZEN still lists file(s) that no longer spread
mutations.note: Proves the baseline can only shrink. Without this the frozen list would be a permanent waiver that no assertion ever revisits.

mutations.name: N3 user-spawn auth-service child loses its COTAL_ strip while another child in the same file still strips
mutations.note: The mixed-file regression: one stripped child plus a comment containing delete used to clear this file. The census must fail on the remaining unstripped spread.

mutations.name: N4 real suite population loses every spread after the first per file
mutations.expectRed: spread enumeration was truncated or the multi-spread population disappeared
mutations.note: Proves the shipped census enumerates the real multi-spread repository population, rather than only satisfying embedded classifier examples.

mutations.name: N5 process.env ownership regresses from structural depth to column zero
mutations.expectRed: a regex close brace must not hide nested scrub depth
mutations.note: Proves structural brace depth remains part of ownership after regex-region tokenization: replacing it with a column-zero test falsely accepts the nested close-brace control.

mutations.name: N6 process.env ownership loses its lexical-region boundary
mutations.find:
strip.region === region &&
      lexical.regions[strip.start] === region &&
      lexical.regions[strip.deleteStart] === region &&
mutations.expectRed: an unused nested template scrub must not clear a module-code spread
mutations.note: Proves scrub ownership cannot cross from a nested or top-level string/template region into module code or another child-script literal.

mutations.name: N7 regex literal braces regain structural meaning
mutations.expectRed: a regex close brace must not hide nested scrub depth
mutations.note: Proves regex-literal tokenization excludes brace data from structural depth while the separate division control remains green at baseline.

mutations.name: N8 template raw text loses its separate lexical region
mutations.expectRed: a raw-template scrub must not clear a spread inside interpolation code
mutations.note: Proves template raw text has a distinct child-script owner while interpolation code keeps the containing region; flattening the two falsely lets raw scrub text license interpolation.

mutations.name: N9 interpolation expressions inherit the template raw-text region
mutations.expectRed: a module scrub must clear a spread inside template interpolation code
mutations.note: Proves interpolation expressions inherit the containing code owner instead of the template raw-text owner.

mutations.name: N10 interpolation contents stop receiving recursive lexical regions
mutations.expectRed: an unused nested template scrub must not clear a module-code spread
mutations.note: Proves nested literals inside interpolation code are recursively discovered and assigned their own child-script regions.

mutations.name: N11 every sibling interpolation receives recursive lexical regions
mutations.expectRed: a nested template scrub must not clear a sibling interpolation spread
mutations.note: Proves recursive parsing covers every interpolation span; parsing only the final span falsely lets a nested scrub clear a spread in an earlier sibling.

mutations.name: N12 child-script source mapping regresses to linear cooked offsets
mutations.expectRed: an escaped child-script scrub must retain its source brace depth
mutations.note: Proves cooked child-script matches retain original source coordinates: a linear cooked offset lands before the closing brace and falsely treats this top-level scrub as nested.
